How to improve the use of computerized physician order-entry systems: an international delphi study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what information can be useful in the delivery of medication alert information within CPOE systems.
the development of a new alert system for the computerized physician order-entry (CPOE), which is based on the concept of context awareness.
the design of a CPOE system that can provide a user with the right information at the right time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CPOE systems should provide the user with a comprehensive overview of the patient's medication and medical history, and that the alert mechanism should be designed to be proactive, to provide the user with information on the clinical situation of the patient, and to provide the user the possibility to easily access information on the strength of evidence on the alert.
CPOE systems should present the following information to the user in the most effective manner: (1) severity, (2) patient clinical status, (3) probability, (4) risk and (5) evidence of the ADE.

CPOE alerting systems should provide the user with a combination of the following information (in order of importance): the clinical status of the user's patient; the severity of the effect the ADE the alerts refer to; the risk factors of the user's patients; the strength of evidence on the basis of which the alert was built; the probability that the ADE the alarm refers to will occur; and finally, the clinical context of the alert.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important context information items for prioritizing and presenting alert messages are the severity of the ADE, clinical status of the patients, probability of the occurrence of an ADE and risk factors of the patients.

the most important context information items are severity and probability of the ADE, and that active alerting, simulation, and a patient medication overview are the best ways to present alert information.

the most important context factors to be presented to users are those that provide information about the potential severity of an ADE, the probability of an ADE to occur and patient-specific information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the context of the patient and the medication order is important in the prioritization of alerts, and that alert delivery methods should be tailored to the context of use.
